title: Geometric stalks are conservative on the etale topos of an algebraic space
statement: Work in [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $X$ be an algebraic space over a scheme $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space]. For every geometric point $\bar x:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to X$, with $\Omega$ algebraically closed, define $F_{\bar x}$ as the colimit of the sets $F(U)$ over pointed etale scheme neighbourhoods $(U,\bar u)$ of $\bar x$. This defines a functor $\operatorname{Sh}(X_{\mathrm{et}})\to\operatorname{Sets}$ preserving finite limits and all small colimits. A map $F\to G$ of sheaves of sets is a monomorphism, respectively an epimorphism, respectively an isomorphism, if and only if every geometric stalk map is injective, respectively surjective, respectively bijective. Consequently two sheaf maps agree if their maps on all geometric stalks agree. These assertions include the empty algebraic space, whose sheaf topos has just one object up to isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 04K5 (theorem-exactness-stalks), with the geometric stalk/point construction of section-points; sites.tex, point stalk functors preserve finite limits and colimits.

proof.text: Fix $\bar x$ and use [lem-sfb-space-pointed-etale-neighbourhoods-cofiltered]. Restrictions define $D_F:\mathcal N_{\bar x}^{op}\to\mathbf{Set}$; a sheaf map acts on each representative section, and hence on the colimit, giving the stalk functor. The cited neighbourhood lemma supplies a small filtered opposite index. For any finite diagram of sheaves, [lem-weil-pbc-site-sheaf-sets-limits-sectionwise] computes its limit at $U$ as the limit of section sets. Applying [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimits-commute-finite-limits] therefore identifies the stalk of this limit with the limit of the stalks, including the empty diagram. This proves finite-limit preservation.

For a set $A$ put $L(U)=\operatorname{Hom}_X(\operatorname{Spec}\Omega,U)$ and $P_A(U)=\operatorname{Map}(L(U),A)$, with restriction by precomposition. This is a sheaf: for a covering $\{U_i\to U\}$, every $l\in L(U)$ lifts to an $l_i\in L(U_i)$ by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-cover-geometric-point-lift], since the covering is a jointly surjective etale family of schemes. Matching functions glue by $a(l)=a_i(l_i)$; two choices give a lift to $U_i\times_U U_j$ by [def-pc-fibre-product], so matching makes this independent of choices and unique. This verifies exactly the sheaf condition, even when $L(U)$ is empty. The universal property of the colimit gives inverse natural bijections $\operatorname{Map}(F_{\bar x},A)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(F,P_A)$: send $b$ to $s\mapsto(l\mapsto b([U,l,s]))$; send $\alpha$ to $[U,l,s]\mapsto\alpha_U(s)(l)$. Naturality of $\alpha$ says the latter respects each restriction relation. Thus the stalk functor is left adjoint to $A\mapsto P_A$.

source.place: spaces-properties.tex Tag 04K0 (lemma-stalk-gives-point); sites.tex Tag 00Y8 (lemma-point-pushforward-sheaf), with the adjunction and gluing written out.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-left-adjoint-preserves-colimits] to the adjunction in step 2. For every small diagram admitting a colimit in the sheaf category, its image cocone is a colimit cocone of sets. This proves preservation of all small colimits in the categorical sense, without substituting an objectwise presheaf colimit for the sheaf colimit.

If $a:F\to G$ is mono, its diagonal $d:F\to F\times_G F$ is invertible: the two projections agree since their composites with $a$ agree, and either projection is inverse to $d$. By step 1, $d_{\bar x}$ is the diagonal $F_{\bar x}\to F_{\bar x}\times_{G_{\bar x}}F_{\bar x}$, so it is bijective. The diagonal of a set map is bijective exactly when that map is injective. Thus every $a_{\bar x}$ is injective. The required sheaf fibre product exists by the cited limits node.

Conversely assume every $a_{\bar x}$ injective. If $s,t\in F(U)$ have $a(s)=a(t)$, choose for each $u\in U$ an algebraic closure of $\kappa(u)$ and its geometric point $\bar u$ of $U$, using [lem-pc-algebraic-closure-exists-unique] and [def-weil-geometric-point]. Compose to $\bar x$ on $X$. The germs of $s,t$ in $F_{\bar x}$ are equal. By [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-sets-elementwise](3) and the cofiltered-neighbourhood node, they become equal on some pointed refinement $V\to U$. This is etale by [lem-trf-space-chartwise-etale-permanence], since both $V,U$ are etale over $X$, and its image contains $u$. The family of all such refinements is a covering of $U$ by [def-trf-algebraic-space]; it is a set in the fixed small-site universe. Sheaf separatedness gives $s=t$. Thus all component maps of $a$ are injective, which makes $a$ mono: equality after $a$ of two natural transformations is equality at each section. For $U$ empty the empty covering gives the same separatedness argument.

source.place: Tag 04K5 (theorem-exactness-stalks), injectivity proof expanded using the filtered-colimit description after Tag 04JY.

proof.text: If $a$ is epi, [lem-weil-pbc-site-sheaf-sets-epi-locally-surjective] supplies local lifts of every $t\in G(U)$. Given a stalk element, represent it by $(U,\bar u,t)$ using [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-sets-elementwise] and the cofiltered-neighbourhood node. Choose a covering $\{U_i\to U\}$ and sections lifting $t|_{U_i}$. By [lem-weil-pbc-etale-cover-geometric-point-lift], $\bar u$ lifts to some $U_i$ with the same field. The corresponding lifted section represents a preimage of the original stalk element. Hence $a_{\bar x}$ is surjective.

source.place: Tag 04K5 (theorem-exactness-stalks), surjectivity; etale-cohomology.tex Tag 03PR (lemma-geometric-lift-to-cover); sites.tex Tag 00WN (lemma-mono-epi-sheaves).

proof.text: Assume instead all $a_{\bar x}$ surjective, and take $t\in G(U)$. For each $u\in U$, choose $\bar u$ using the algebraic-closure and geometric-point nodes as in step 5 and put $\bar x=\bar u\to X$. Choose a preimage in $F_{\bar x}$ of the germ of $t$. The elementwise filtered-colimit node represents it on a pointed neighbourhood $V$ and represents equality of its image with $t$ on a common pointed refinement $W\to V,U$. Thus there is $s\in F(W)$ with $a(s)=t|_W$. The map $W\to U$ is etale by the permanence node and hits $u$. All such refinements form a covering by the small-site covering definition. For empty $U$ take the empty covering. This gives local surjectivity, hence $a$ is epi by the cited epi characterization.

source.place: Tag 04K5 (theorem-exactness-stalks), surjectivity proof expanded using the filtered-colimit description after Tag 04JY.

proof.text: An isomorphism gives bijective stalk maps by functoriality. Conversely bijective stalks give both sectionwise injectivity (step 5) and local surjectivity (step 7). For $t\in G(U)$ choose local lifts $s_i\in F(U_i)$. On $U_i\times_U U_j$ their images are both the restriction of $t$, so sectionwise injectivity makes the lifts agree. The sheaf condition glues them uniquely to $s\in F(U)$ with $a(s)=t$; this equality is checked on the covering by separatedness of $G$. Thus every component of $a$ is bijective. The component inverses are natural by applying the naturality identity of $a$ and cancelling its bijective components. Hence $a$ is an isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 04K5 (theorem-exactness-stalks); sites.tex Tag 00WN (lemma-mono-epi-sheaves), bijectivity assertion expanded by gluing.

proof.text: For maps $a,b:F\to G$ agreeing on all stalks, let $e:E\to F$ be their equalizer, which exists by [lem-weil-pbc-site-sheaf-sets-limits-sectionwise]. Step 1 identifies $e_{\bar x}$ with the equalizer of the equal maps $a_{\bar x},b_{\bar x}$, hence a bijection. Step 8 makes $e$ invertible; from $ae=be$ obtain $a=b$.

If $X=\varnothing$, every scheme $U\to X$ is empty, and the empty family covers it by the jointly-surjective covering definition in [def-trf-algebraic-space]. The sheaf equalizer condition in [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology] forces $F(U)$ to be a singleton, since both products indexed by the empty covering are singletons. Every sheaf is therefore uniquely isomorphic to the singleton sheaf and every morphism is invertible; parallel morphisms agree. There are no geometric points, so all the stalkwise tests are vacuous, as required.

lean.statement: theorem etaleGeometricStalks_conservative {S : Scheme.{u}} (X : AlgebraicSpace S) : (∀ (Ω : Type u) [Field Ω] [IsAlgClosed Ω] (b : Spec (.of Ω) ⟶ S) (x : yoneda.obj (Over.mk b) ⟶ X.obj.obj), PreservesFiniteLimits (X.pointedSetStalk.{u, w} x) ∧ PreservesColimitsOfSize.{max (u + 1) w, max (u + 1) w} (X.pointedSetStalk.{u, w} x)) ∧ (∀ (F G : Sheaf X.etaleTopology (Type (max (u + 1) w))) (α : F ⟶ G), (Mono α ↔ ∀ (Ω : Type u) [Field Ω] [IsAlgClosed Ω] (b : Spec (.of Ω) ⟶ S) (x : yoneda.obj (Over.mk b) ⟶ X.obj.obj), Function.Injective ((X.pointedSetStalk x).map α)) ∧ (Epi α ↔ ∀ (Ω : Type u) [Field Ω] [IsAlgClosed Ω] (b : Spec (.of Ω) ⟶ S) (x : yoneda.obj (Over.mk b) ⟶ X.obj.obj), Function.Surjective ((X.pointedSetStalk x).map α)) ∧ (IsIso α ↔ ∀ (Ω : Type u) [Field Ω] [IsAlgClosed Ω] (b : Spec (.of Ω) ⟶ S) (x : yoneda.obj (Over.mk b) ⟶ X.obj.obj), Function.Bijective ((X.pointedSetStalk x).map α))) ∧ (∀ (F G : Sheaf X.etaleTopology (Type (max (u + 1) w))) (α β : F ⟶ G), (∀ (Ω : Type u) [Field Ω] [IsAlgClosed Ω] (b : Spec (.of Ω) ⟶ S) (x : yoneda.obj (Over.mk b) ⟶ X.obj.obj), (X.pointedSetStalk x).map α = (X.pointedSetStalk x).map β) → α = β) ∧ ((∀ U : X.EtaleSite, IsEmpty ((X.etaleForget).obj U)) → ∀ F G : Sheaf X.etaleTopology (Type (max (u + 1) w)), Nonempty (F ≅ G))
